name: Language-Learning Apps
description: Size the market for subscription language-learning apps.
formula: SOM = Population x Penetration Rate x Purchase Frequency x Average Spend x Serviceable % x Obtainable Share %
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
Step 5: Calculate SAM = TAM x serviceable_pct
Step 6: Calculate SOM = SAM x obtainable_share_pct
key_insight: This is a subscription market (months/year times $/month), and the addressable segment -- adults actively learning a language right now -- is much smaller than "anyone who might someday want to learn."
common_mistakes: Sizing all adults instead of those actively learning a language today
Forgetting to annualize monthly subscription spend (x12)
Ignoring obtainable share in a category with several dominant incumbents already serving this demand
framework_soundbite: Actively learning, subscribed monthly, split against the incumbents already in this space -- not everyone who's ever thought about learning a language.
business_contexts: a language-learning app evaluating a new market launch
an edtech investor sizing the language-learning subscription market
question_patterns: A language-learning app is deciding whether to launch in a new country and wants to size the annual subscription revenue it could realistically capture against local competitors.

serviceable_pct.unit: % within the new country's launch reach

prompts.advanced: An edtech investor is evaluating a language-learning app whose international expansion plan assumes conversion rates the fund's own data team hasn't been able to validate against comparable markets. Build an independent serviceable-obtainable-market estimate before the board vote.
prompts.beginner: Estimate the serviceable obtainable market for subscription language-learning apps in a new country launch, accounting for realistic competitive capture.
prompts.intermediate: A language-learning app is deciding whether to launch in a new country and wants to size the annual subscription revenue it could realistically capture against local competitors.
